title: Hosted API: queue amplification diagnosis and rate-smoothing shim
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: A top-tier customer reported intermittent spikes of 500s and timeouts during a peak embedding upload window. The immediate visible pattern was a burst of similar requests that coincided with a downstream model autoscaler event. Initial triage suggests request queuing on the edge combined with connection pool reset behavior led to amplified retries and head-of-line blocking. This ticket captures the diagnosis, a low-risk hotpatch (rate-smoothing shim + request flattening), and observability uplift required to prevent recurrence.
investigation_findings: Spike timeline: anomalies started 2025-02-09 22:13 UTC after a scheduled model variant autoscale event.
Edge proxy queuing: per-host request queue length increased, exposing a head-of-line blocking pattern where long-running requests delayed many short requests.
Connection pool reset bug: evidence that the pool returned connections to an incorrect idle state during transient TLS renegotiation, causing slow reconnects and reducing available in-flight slots.
Amplification loop: client SDK retries (default aggressive backoff) replayed similar requests rapidly while upstream queueing persisted, multiplying load on backend workers.
Hot-cold interaction: a large batched embedding job plus an autoscaler add created transient tail latencies that propagated to the edge where admission logic lacked smoothing.
Observability gaps: missing per-route in-flight metrics, no short-lived request fingerprinting to detect identical concurrent requests.
Hypothesis: rate-smoothing at the edge + request coalescing (short TTL) will prevent amplification while we fix connection pool reset and tune SDK backoff defaults.
action_items: Implement edge rate-smoothing shim: limit bursts by smoothing inflow to backend per-route over a 500ms window (config flag, default off).
Add request flattening: coalesce identical requests with same idempotency/fingerprint for 200ms with single upstream execution and shared response.
Emergency config rollout: toggle per-tenant in-flight cap to 50% for high-volume tenants while monitoring error rate impact.
Fix connection pool reset logic in proxy: ensure TLS renegotiation moves connection to idle only after successful handshake (PR drafted).
Change SDK defaults: reduce retry aggressiveness for transient 5xx to avoid quick replays (align with graceful jitter).
Observability uplift: add per-route in-flight gauges, request fingerprint histogram, and a dashboard with tail-percentile latency and coalesce hit-rate.
Postmortem and runbook: document incident triggers, mitigation knobs, and customer comms template.
E2E test: synthetic tenant surge harness to validate smoothing/coalesce under 2k rps for embeddings flows.
acceptance_criteria: Edge rate-smoothing feature implemented behind feature flag and can be toggled per-tenant via Console.
Request coalescing implemented with transparent response sharing; coalesced hit-rate >= 20% in synthetic test and no customer-visible regressions.
Connection pool reset bug fixed with unit + integration tests proving no connection starvation after TLS renegotiation.
Dashboard shows per-route in-flight, coalesce hit-rate, retry amplification ratio, and alerts fire at configurable thresholds.
SDK patch released (minor) and communicated to customers with recommended backoff settings; gradual rollout plan in place.
Runbook updated and reviewed by SRE and Support; on-call can enable smoothing and caps within 5 minutes.
implementation_steps: (A) Prototype rate-smoothing in edge service using token-bucket with leaky-window smoothing and feature flag.
(B) Implement in-memory request fingerprint cache (200ms TTL) to dedupe upstream calls for identical payloads.
(C) Add metrics: coalesce_hits, coalesce_misses, per_route_inflight, retry_amplification_ratio; wire to Grafana.
(D) Roll hotpatch to Canary tenants, observe for 2 hours, then ramp to 20% tenants based on error-rate delta.
(E) Land connection-pool reset fix in proxy, run integration tests with TLS renegotiation simulator, then stage deploy.
(F) Coordinate with SDK team to publish reduced-retry defaults and communicate breaking/non-breaking changes.
(G) Run synthetic load test (embedding pattern) and validate acceptance criteria.
(H) Close ticket after postmortem and handover to reliability roadmap for permanent fixes.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: coalescing may increase tail latency for skewed requests if the first request is slow. Mitigation: short TTL (200ms) and per-route opt-out.
Risk: smoothing could throttle legitimate bursty workloads for some customers. Mitigation: per-tenant exemption list and gradual ramp with metrics-based gate.
Risk: SDK changes might break ad-hoc retry patterns. Mitigation: minor-version release, clear migration notes, and extended beta for enterprise customers.
